posts.author: Dutchelm05
posts.content_md:
Greetings all,

I'm sure this topic has been brought up before. My attempts in finding something on the subject have been futile.

I was showing someone a hologram and only had a flashlight handy. It was a mini-mag (I think they may be Krypton). The image replay was blurring and poor. I later started looking for various light sources including white light LEDs, halogen and incandescent light sources. It seemed that flashlight sources are poor while lights (even frosted lights) that are several meters away are fine.

Can the collective wisdom tell me what the requirements for lighting are? I am especially interested in close proximity lights for a home display. Diffused light, point source lights? If this has already been discussed please direct me to the link.

Thanks all and peace.

Tony

posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.content_md:
A point source at the exact placement of the spatial filters pinhole is the best place in theory. You will find that shrinking or expanding the fringes will move that. Here is an interesting link:

[http://rudieberkhout.home.mindspring.co ... isplay.htm](http://rudieberkhout.home.mindspring.com/SPIE-Acompactdisplay.htm)

For reflection holograms I like leds. I hang them from the ceiling.

I will mostly have more questions later.

posts.author: Tom B.
posts.content_md:
I like LEDs too. When the LED is the same color as the holo, the contrast can be very good and the apparent brightness even for dimmish Denisyuks can be quite acceptable. I find Amber to be the least objectionable color for wall display and tune my holos to match. Red is too alarming, Green is too garish, Blue might be nice but clean, high contrast blue holos are not exactly easy to find or make.

Many LED lamps use multiple small LEDs which is bad, producing a blurry image. The preferred type uses a single high-power LED. OptiLeds are of this type and produce a very clean, narrow beam, good for lighting 4X5 holos from as close as 2-3 feet or bigger ones from further away. Some sources:

[http://www.laserreflections.com/LED.htm](http://www.laserreflections.com/LED.htm) (Most of my LEDS came from here)

[http://www.lightworld.com/](http://www.lightworld.com/) Have not tried these guys yet, but they claim to offer OptiLeds too

Most of my gallery pics used OptiLed ambers for lighting - [http://members.shaw.ca/holopix/My_holograms.html](http://members.shaw.ca/holopix/My_holograms.html)
